Test a broad weighted combination on the full pool to see if including all models improves over the selective pool, given the trend-dominated, high predictability series.
test a median combination over the full pool to see if a robust central tendency helps with the trend-dominated, moderately ranked series.
test a per‑horizon weighted approach with softmax_neg_error on the full pool to see if a softer weighting improves over the hard inverse_error.
The series is trend‑dominated with moderate ranking stability; a selective trimmed mean over the strongest models (pool4) may reduce influence of outliers while keeping the best performers.
I will try a selective DBA combination on the high‑performance pool4 to see if a constrained optimization can beat the trimmed mean.
try a different weighting scheme (softmax_neg_error) on the selective pool4 to see if a smoother weight improves over trimmed mean.
The series is trend‑dominated with moderate ranking stability; a robust central tendency may help. Try a median combination over the selective pool4.
Explore a simple mean combination on the selective pool4 to see if a non‑weighted average outperforms the trimmed mean, given the strong trend and moderate ranking stability.
test a selective weighted combination on the smaller pool5, which may improve over pool4 by removing some correlated models.
test a per‑horizon‑aware weighted combo on a smaller, less correlated pool5, using softmax_neg_error to give higher weight to lower‑error models at each step.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.133. Series context: trend strength 0.9994 and seasonal strength 0.0529; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.571); 7 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 37.534.
